title: Narrative Relativity: Emotional Continuity vs. Physical Accuracy
use_cases: Use when maintaining plot coherence in time-travel stories with complex geometries
Implement when balancing character motivations against scientific plausibility
Configure when modeling environmental reconfiguration around anomalous elements
Apply when designing emotional pacing to act as a narrative speed limit
Utilize to ensure that magic or advanced tech behaves as ecosystem forces rather than isolated decorations
content:
Einstein reshaped our understanding of time. Fiction reshapes it further.

![](https://fictionphile.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/russian-1024x576.jpg)

In time-travel stories such as Arrival or Russian Dolls, the timeline contorts into impossible geometries, yet audiences remain grounded because the characters’ motivations remain constant. Emotional continuity becomes the speed limit of narrative relativity.

This is why Interstellar resonates even when the science wobbles. Cooper’s love for his daughter creates an emotional gravity well strong enough to pull the entire plot into coherence.

In speculative fiction, emotion becomes the universal constant. Break it, and no amount of accurate physics will save you.

The strongest worldbuilding treats impossible elements not as decorations, but as ecological forces. Introduce one anomaly into a system, and the entire environment must reconfigure around it. Magic, advanced technology, monsters, or miracles don’t exist in isolation. They behave like invasive species or new energy sources, reshaping everything they touch.

This is why some speculative worlds feel thin while others feel inevitable. The difference is consequence.
